answers.explanation: 48 bits, written as 6 bytes or 12 hex digits.
Organizationally Unique Identifier, assigned to the manufacturer by the IEEE.
Media Access Control. Layer 2 is sometimes called the MAC layer for that reason.
All 48 bits set to 1. Every NIC on the LAN accepts a frame sent to it.
Windows uses dashes and capitals, Cisco uses dotted groups of four, but the 48 bits are the same.
The second hex digit is a (1010 in binary), so the locally administered bit is set and the multicast bit isn't.
A burned-in MAC address stays the same. (A random private address is a deliberate exception, chosen per network to resist tracking.)
Windows calls it the Physical Address. Linux's ifconfig shows HWaddr or ether, and macOS lists it under Hardware.
A fixed MAC address is a fixed identifier every network sees. Randomizing it per network breaks that link.
